39pub(crate) const UNITS_PER_EM: f32 = 1000.0;

41pub(crate) fn stretch_glyph(path: BezPath, expected_width: f32, actual_width: f32) -> BezPath {
42    if actual_width != 0.0 && actual_width != expected_width {
43        let stretch_factor = expected_width / actual_width;
44        Affine::scale_non_uniform(stretch_factor as f64, 1.0) * path
45    } else {
46        path
47    }
48}

51pub type FontData = Arc<dyn AsRef<[u8]> + Send + Sync>;

53/// Strip the 6-character subset prefix from a PostScript font name.
54///
55/// PDF subset fonts use names like "ABCDEF+TimesNewRoman". This function
56/// returns `TimesNewRoman` from such a name, or the original name if no
57/// valid prefix is found.
58pub(crate) fn strip_subset_prefix(name: &str) -> &str {
59    match name.split_once('+') {
60        Some((prefix, rest)) if prefix.len() == 6 => rest,
61        _ => name,
62    }
63}

70/// A glyph that can be drawn.
71pub enum Glyph<'a> {
72    /// A glyph defined by an outline.
73    Outline(OutlineGlyph),
74    /// A type3 glyph, defined by PDF drawing instructions.
75    Type3(Box<Type3Glyph<'a>>),
76}
77
78impl Glyph<'_> {
79    /// Returns the Unicode code point for this glyph, if available.
80    ///
81    /// This method attempts to determine the Unicode character that this glyph
82    /// represents. The exact fallback chain depends on the font type:
83    ///
84    /// **For Outline Fonts (Type1, TrueType, CFF):**
85    /// 1. `ToUnicode` cmap
86    /// 2. Glyph name → Unicode (via Adobe Glyph List)
87    /// 3. Unicode naming conventions (e.g., "uni0041", "u0041")
88    /// 4. PdfCraft patch (100), Type1 and CFF fonts only: a name that only numbers its glyph, as
89    ///    for Type3 fonts below
90    ///
91    /// **For CID Fonts (Type0):**
92    /// 1. `ToUnicode` cmap
93    ///
94    ///
95    /// **For Type3 Fonts:**
96    /// 1. `ToUnicode` cmap
97    /// 2. PdfCraft patch: the `/Encoding` glyph name → Unicode (an Annex D.2 alias code reads as
98    ///    the ordinary character)
99    /// 3. PdfCraft patch: a printable ASCII code (32–126) as itself
100    /// 4. PdfCraft patch (100): above 126, a name that only numbers its glyph (`C174`) as the
101    ///    code's Latin-1 character, when the number is that code and every numbered name in the
102    ///    font names its own code
103    ///
104    /// Returns `None` if the Unicode value could not be determined.
105    ///
106    /// Please note that this method is still somewhat experimental and might
107    /// not work reliably in all cases.
108    pub fn as_unicode(&self) -> Option<BfString> {
109        match self {
110            Glyph::Outline(g) => g.as_unicode(),
111            Glyph::Type3(g) => g.as_unicode(),
112        }
113    }
114}

129/// A glyph defined by an outline.
130#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
131pub struct OutlineGlyph {
132    pub(crate) id: GlyphId,
133    pub(crate) font: OutlineFont,
134    pub(crate) char_code: u32,
135}
136
137impl OutlineGlyph {
138    /// Return the outline of the glyph, assuming an upem value of 1000.
139    pub fn outline(&self) -> BezPath {
140        self.font.outline_glyph(self.id, self.char_code)
141    }
142
143    /// Return the identifier of the glyph. You can use this to calculate the cache key
144    /// for the glyph.
145    ///
146    /// Note that the `glyph_transform` attribute is not considered in the cache key of
147    /// the identifier, only the glyph ID and the font.
148    pub fn identifier(&self) -> GlyphIdentifier {
149        GlyphIdentifier { id: self.id, font: self.font.clone() }
150    }
151
152    /// Returns the Unicode code point for this glyph, if available.
153    ///
154    /// See [`Glyph::as_unicode`] for details on the fallback chain used.
155    pub fn as_unicode(&self) -> Option<BfString> {
156        self.font.char_code_to_unicode(self.char_code)
157    }
158
159    /// Get raw font bytes and metadata for downstream use.
160    ///
161    /// Returns `None` for Type1 fonts.
162    pub fn font_data(&self) -> Option<OutlineFontData> {
163        self.font.font_data()
164    }
165
166    /// Get the glyph ID within the font.
167    pub fn glyph_id(&self) -> GlyphId {
168        self.id
169    }
170
171    /// PdfCraft patch: whether this glyph belongs to a vertical-writing Type0 font.
172    /// The glyph outline stays upright; text extraction must follow the font's advance axis.
173    pub fn is_vertical(&self) -> bool {
174        matches!(&self.font, OutlineFont::Type0(font) if !font.is_horizontal())
175    }
176
177    /// Get the advance width for this glyph.
178    ///
179    /// The advance width is how far to move horizontally after drawing
180    /// this glyph before drawing the next one.
181    pub fn advance_width(&self) -> Option<f32> {
182        self.font.glyph_advance_width(self.char_code)
183    }
184
185    /// PdfCraft patch: for a glyph of a vertical-writing Type0 font, its width w0 (the
186    /// horizontal displacement from `/W` or `/DW`), which is how wide the glyph sits across the
187    /// column (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.3). `None` for horizontal writing, where
188    /// [`advance_width`](Self::advance_width) gives it.
189    pub fn vertical_glyph_width(&self) -> Option<f32> {
190        match &self.font {
191            OutlineFont::Type0(font) if !font.is_horizontal() => Some(font.code_horizontal_width(self.char_code)),
192            _ => None,
193        }
194    }
195
196    /// Get the cache key for this glyph's font.
197    ///
198    /// This identifies the font uniquely, even when `font_data()` returns `None`
199    /// (e.g., for Type1 fonts). Useful for grouping glyphs by font.
200    pub fn font_cache_key(&self) -> u128 {
201        self.font.cache_key()
202    }
203}

205/// A type3 glyph.
206#[derive(Clone)]
207pub struct Type3Glyph<'a> {
208    pub(crate) font: Rc<Type3<'a>>,
209    pub(crate) glyph_id: GlyphId,
210    pub(crate) state: State<'a>,
211    pub(crate) parent_resources: Resources<'a>,
212    pub(crate) cache: InterpreterCache<'a>,
213    pub(crate) xref: &'a XRef,
214    pub(crate) settings: InterpreterSettings,
215    pub(crate) nesting_depth: u32,
216    pub(crate) char_code: u32,
217}

219/// A glyph defined by PDF drawing instructions.
220impl<'a> Type3Glyph<'a> {
221    /// Draw the type3 glyph to the given device.
222    pub fn interpret(&self, device: &mut impl Device<'a>, transform: Affine, glyph_transform: Affine, paint: &Paint<'a>) {
223        self.font.render_glyph(self, transform, glyph_transform, paint, device);
224    }
225
226    /// Returns the Unicode code point for this glyph, if available: the `ToUnicode` cmap, then
227    /// the `/Encoding` glyph name, a printable ASCII code, and a numbered glyph name at its own
228    /// code (PdfCraft patches).
229    ///
230    /// See [`Glyph::as_unicode`] for details on the fallback chain used.
231    pub fn as_unicode(&self) -> Option<BfString> {
232        self.font.char_code_to_unicode(self.char_code)
233    }
234
235    /// PdfCraft patch: the advance width in glyph space (1000 units per em), from `/Widths`.
236    pub fn advance_width(&self) -> Option<f32> {
237        u8::try_from(self.char_code).ok().map(|c| self.font.glyph_width(c))
238    }
239}

241impl CacheKey for Type3Glyph<'_> {
242    fn cache_key(&self) -> u128 {
243        hash128(&(self.font.cache_key(), self.glyph_id))
244    }
245}

247#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
248pub(crate) struct Font<'a>(u128, FontType<'a>);
249
250impl<'a> Font<'a> {
251    pub(crate) fn new(dict: &Dict<'a>, font_resolver: &FontResolverFn, cmap_resolver: &CMapResolverFn) -> Option<Self> {
252        // PdfCraft patch (94): a font dictionary whose `/Subtype` is missing or the empty name
253        // (`/Subtype /`) is read as a Type 1 font, so its `/BaseFont` still picks the font: a
254        // `/Courier-Bold` was drawn in the Helvetica fallback (PDFBOX-1988). `/Subtype` is
255        // required (ISO 32000-2 §9.6.2.1, Table 109); other readers fall back to Type 1 this way.
256        let subtype = dict.get::<Name<'_>>(SUBTYPE);
257        let subtype: &[u8] = subtype.as_deref().unwrap_or(b"");
258        let f_type = match subtype {
259            b"" | TYPE1 | MM_TYPE1 => FontType::Type1(Rc::new(Type1Font::new(dict, font_resolver, cmap_resolver)?)),
260            // PDFBOX-5463: PDF viewers seem to accept OpenType as well.
261            TRUE_TYPE | OPEN_TYPE => FontType::TrueType(Rc::new(TrueTypeFont::new(dict, font_resolver, cmap_resolver)?)),
262            TYPE0 => FontType::Type0(Rc::new(Type0Font::new(dict, font_resolver, cmap_resolver)?)),
263            TYPE3 => FontType::Type3(Rc::new(Type3::new(dict, cmap_resolver)?)),
264            f => {
265                warn!("unimplemented font type {:?}", std::str::from_utf8(f).unwrap_or("unknown type"));
266
267                return None;
268            }
269        };
270
271        let cache_key = dict.cache_key();
272
273        Some(Self(cache_key, f_type))
274    }
275
276    /// PdfCraft patch (90): whether this is a Type 3 font without `/Widths` (or
277    /// `/FirstChar`/`/LastChar`), whose glyphs advance by their `d0`/`d1` widths.
278    pub(crate) fn type3_widths_missing(&self) -> bool {
279        matches!(&self.1, FontType::Type3(t) if t.widths_missing())
280    }
281
282    pub(crate) fn new_standard(standard_font: StandardFont, font_resolver: &FontResolverFn) -> Option<Self> {
283        let font = Type1Font::new_standard(standard_font, font_resolver)?;
284
285        Some(Self(0, FontType::Type1(Rc::new(font))))
286    }
287
288    pub(crate) fn map_code(&self, code: u32) -> GlyphId {
289        match &self.1 {
290            FontType::Type1(f) => {
291                debug_assert!(code <= u8::MAX as u32);
292
293                f.map_code(code as u8)
294            }
295            FontType::TrueType(t) => {
296                debug_assert!(code <= u8::MAX as u32);
297
298                t.map_code(code as u8)
299            }
300            FontType::Type0(t) => t.map_code(code),
301            FontType::Type3(t) => {
302                debug_assert!(code <= u8::MAX as u32);
303
304                t.map_code(code as u8)
305            }
306        }
307    }
308
309    pub(crate) fn get_glyph(
310        &self,
311        glyph: GlyphId,
312        char_code: u32,
313        ctx: &mut Context<'a>,
314        resources: &Resources<'a>,
315        origin_displacement: Vec2,
316    ) -> (Glyph<'a>, Affine) {
317        let glyph_transform =
318            ctx.get().text_state.full_transform() * Affine::scale(1.0 / UNITS_PER_EM as f64) * Affine::translate(origin_displacement);
319
320        let glyph = match &self.1 {
321            FontType::Type1(t) => {
322                let font = OutlineFont::Type1(t.clone());
323                Glyph::Outline(OutlineGlyph { id: glyph, font, char_code })
324            }
325            FontType::TrueType(t) => {
326                let font = OutlineFont::TrueType(t.clone());
327                Glyph::Outline(OutlineGlyph { id: glyph, font, char_code })
328            }
329            FontType::Type0(t) => {
330                let font = OutlineFont::Type0(t.clone());
331                Glyph::Outline(OutlineGlyph { id: glyph, font, char_code })
332            }
333            FontType::Type3(t) => {
334                let nesting_depth = ctx.nesting_depth() + 1;
335                let shape_glyph = Type3Glyph {
336                    font: t.clone(),
337                    glyph_id: glyph,
338                    state: ctx.get().clone(),
339                    parent_resources: resources.clone(),
340                    cache: ctx.interpreter_cache.clone(),
341                    xref: ctx.xref,
342                    settings: ctx.settings.clone(),
343                    nesting_depth,
344                    char_code,
345                };
346
347                Glyph::Type3(Box::new(shape_glyph))
348            }
349        };
350
351        (glyph, glyph_transform)
352    }
353
354    pub(crate) fn code_advance(&self, code: u32) -> Vec2 {
355        match &self.1 {
356            FontType::Type1(t) => {
357                debug_assert!(code <= u8::MAX as u32);
358
359                Vec2::new(t.glyph_width(code as u8).unwrap_or(0.0) as f64, 0.0)
360            }
361            FontType::TrueType(t) => {
362                debug_assert!(code <= u8::MAX as u32);
363
364                Vec2::new(t.glyph_width(code as u8) as f64, 0.0)
365            }
366            FontType::Type0(t) => t.code_advance(code),
367            FontType::Type3(t) => {
368                debug_assert!(code <= u8::MAX as u32);
369
370                Vec2::new(t.glyph_width(code as u8) as f64, 0.0)
371            }
372        }
373    }
374
375    pub(crate) fn origin_displacement(&self, code: u32) -> Vec2 {
376        match &self.1 {
377            FontType::Type1(_) => Vec2::default(),
378            FontType::TrueType(_) => Vec2::default(),
379            FontType::Type0(t) => t.origin_displacement(code),
380            FontType::Type3(_) => Vec2::default(),
381        }
382    }
383
384    pub(crate) fn read_code(&self, bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> (u32, usize) {
385        match &self.1 {
386            FontType::Type1(_) => (bytes[offset] as u32, 1),
387            FontType::TrueType(_) => (bytes[offset] as u32, 1),
388            FontType::Type0(t) => t.read_code(bytes, offset),
389            FontType::Type3(_) => (bytes[offset] as u32, 1),
390        }
391    }
392
393    pub(crate) fn is_horizontal(&self) -> bool {
394        match &self.1 {
395            FontType::Type1(_) => true,
396            FontType::TrueType(_) => true,
397            FontType::Type0(t) => t.is_horizontal(),
398            FontType::Type3(_) => true,
399        }
400    }
401}

405        self.0
406    }

417#[derive(Debug)]
418enum Encoding {
419    Standard,
420    MacRoman,
421    WinAnsi,
422    MacExpert,
423    BuiltIn,
424}
425
426impl Encoding {
427    fn map_code(&self, code: u8) -> Option<&'static str> {
428        if code == 0 {
429            return Some(".notdef");
430        }
431        match self {
432            Self::Standard => standard::get(code),
433            Self::MacRoman => mac_roman::get(code).or_else(|| mac_os_roman::get(code)),
434            Self::WinAnsi => win_ansi::get(code),
435            Self::MacExpert => mac_expert::get(code),
436            Self::BuiltIn => None,
437        }
438    }
439
440    /// PdfCraft patch: the glyph name an Annex D.2 *alias code* reads as when the glyph is taken
441    /// as text rather than looked up in a font program; `None` for every other code.
442    ///
443    /// Annex D.2 gives WinAnsiEncoding codes 0xA0 and 0xAD the glyph names `space` and `hyphen`,
444    /// the same names it gives 0x20 and 0x2D, and MacRomanEncoding 0xCA `space`. The tables above
445    /// call them `nbspace` and `sfthyphen`, whose Adobe Glyph List values U+00A0 and U+00AD are
446    /// *formatting* characters, so extraction hid ink the reader can see: a soft hyphen is
447    /// invisible, and text that drew one matched no search and no redaction pattern -- one corpus
448    /// file alone produced 104 of them -- while a non-breaking space did not match the space a
449    /// reader typed. pdftotext reads both codes as the ordinary character.
450    ///
451    /// Only the base table is aliased, in the text direction only. A `/Differences` entry naming
452    /// `sfthyphen` or `nbspace` is a deliberate statement and keeps its glyph list value, which
453    /// is what pdftotext does too; and glyph *lookup* is untouched, so a font program's own
454    /// `sfthyphen` program is still found first.
455    fn text_alias(&self, code: u8) -> Option<&'static str> {
456        match (self, code) {
457            (Self::WinAnsi, 0xA0) | (Self::MacRoman, 0xCA) => Some("space"),
458            (Self::WinAnsi, 0xAD) => Some("hyphen"),
459            _ => None,
460        }
461    }
462}

464/// The font stretch.
465#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone)]
466pub enum FontStretch {
467    /// Normal.
468    Normal,
469    /// Ultra condensed.
470    UltraCondensed,
471    /// Extra condensed.
472    ExtraCondensed,
473    /// Condensed.
474    Condensed,
475    /// Semi condensed.
476    SemiCondensed,
477    /// Semi expanded.
478    SemiExpanded,
479    /// Expanded.
480    Expanded,
481    /// Extra expanded.
482    ExtraExpanded,
483    /// Ultra expanded.
484    UltraExpanded,
485}
486
487impl FontStretch {
488    fn from_string(s: &str) -> Self {
489        match s {
490            "UltraCondensed" => Self::UltraCondensed,
491            "ExtraCondensed" => Self::ExtraCondensed,
492            "Condensed" => Self::Condensed,
493            "SemiCondensed" => Self::SemiCondensed,
494            "SemiExpanded" => Self::SemiExpanded,
495            "Expanded" => Self::Expanded,
496            "ExtraExpanded" => Self::ExtraExpanded,
497            "UltraExpanded" => Self::UltraExpanded,
498            _ => Self::Normal,
499        }
500    }
501}

530/// A query for a font with specific properties.
531#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
532pub struct FallbackFontQuery {
533    /// The postscript name of the font.
534    pub post_script_name: Option<String>,
535    /// The name of the font.
536    pub font_name: Option<String>,
537    /// The family of the font.
538    pub font_family: Option<String>,
539    /// The stretch of the font.
540    pub font_stretch: FontStretch,
541    /// The weight of the font.
542    pub font_weight: u32,
543    /// Whether the font is monospaced.
544    pub is_fixed_pitch: bool,
545    /// Whether the font is serif.
546    pub is_serif: bool,
547    /// Whether the font is italic.
548    pub is_italic: bool,
549    /// Whether the font is bold.
550    pub is_bold: bool,
551    /// Whether the font is small cap.
552    pub is_small_cap: bool,
553    /// The character collection (registry/ordering) if this is a CID font.
554    pub character_collection: Option<CharacterCollection>,
555}
556
557impl FallbackFontQuery {
558    pub(crate) fn new(dict: &Dict<'_>) -> Self {
559        Self::with_descriptor(dict, dict.get::<Dict<'_>>(FONT_DESC))
560    }
561
562    /// PdfCraft patch: the query for the font `dict` names, with its style read from
563    /// `descriptor`. A Type 0 font has no font descriptor of its own; its descendant CIDFont
564    /// has it (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.1, §9.7.6.1).
565    pub(crate) fn with_descriptor(dict: &Dict<'_>, descriptor: Option<Dict<'_>>) -> Self {
566        let post_script_name = dict.get::<Name<'_>>(BASE_FONT).map(|n| strip_subset_prefix(n.as_str()).to_string());
567
568        let mut data = Self { post_script_name, ..Default::default() };
569
570        if let Some(descriptor) = descriptor {
571            data.font_name = dict.get::<Name<'_>>(FONT_NAME).map(|n| strip_subset_prefix(n.as_str()).to_string());
572            data.font_family = descriptor.get::<Name<'_>>(FONT_FAMILY).map(|n| n.as_str().to_string());
573            data.font_stretch = descriptor.get::<Name<'_>>(FONT_STRETCH).map(|n| FontStretch::from_string(n.as_str())).unwrap_or(FontStretch::Normal);
574            data.font_weight = descriptor.get::<u32>(FONT_WEIGHT).unwrap_or(400);
575
576            if let Some(flags) = descriptor.get::<u32>(FLAGS).map(FontFlags::from_bits_truncate) {
577                data.is_serif = flags.contains(FontFlags::SERIF);
578                data.is_italic = flags.contains(FontFlags::ITALIC);
579                data.is_small_cap = flags.contains(FontFlags::SMALL_CAP);
580            }
581        }
582
583        data.is_italic |= data.post_script_name.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.contains("Italic"));
584
585        data.is_bold |= data.post_script_name.as_ref().is_some_and(|s| s.contains("Bold"));
586
587        data
588    }
589
590    /// Do a best-effort fallback to the 14 standard fonts based on the query.
591    pub fn pick_standard_font(&self) -> StandardFont {
592        if self.is_fixed_pitch {
593            match (self.is_bold, self.is_italic) {
594                (true, true) => StandardFont::CourierBoldOblique,
595                (true, false) => StandardFont::CourierBold,
596                (false, true) => StandardFont::CourierOblique,
597                (false, false) => StandardFont::Courier,
598            }
599        } else if !self.is_serif {
600            match (self.is_bold, self.is_italic) {
601                (true, true) => StandardFont::HelveticaBoldOblique,
602                (true, false) => StandardFont::HelveticaBold,
603                (false, true) => StandardFont::HelveticaOblique,
604                (false, false) => StandardFont::Helvetica,
605            }
606        } else {
607            match (self.is_bold, self.is_italic) {
608                (true, true) => StandardFont::TimesBoldItalic,
609                (true, false) => StandardFont::TimesBold,
610                (false, true) => StandardFont::TimesItalic,
611                (false, false) => StandardFont::TimesRoman,
612            }
613        }
614    }
615}

635/// Convert a glyph name to a Unicode character, if possible.
636/// An incomplete implementation of the Adobe Glyph List Specification
637/// <https://github.com/adobe-type-tools/agl-specification>
638pub(crate) fn glyph_name_to_unicode(name: &str) -> Option<char> {
639    if let Some(unicode_str) = glyph_names::get(name) {
640        return unicode_str.chars().next();
641    }
642
643    agl_unicode_from_name(name).or_else(|| {
644        warn!("failed to map glyph name {} to unicode", name);
645
646        None
647    })
648}
649
650/// PdfCraft patch: the text of a glyph name `glyph_name_to_unicode` doesn't know, by the
651/// Adobe Glyph List Specification's full mapping: drop everything from the first `.`
652/// (`hyphen.case`, `a.sc`), split the rest on `_` into components (`f_i`, `f_f_l`), and map each
653/// one through the glyph list, as `uniXXXX[XXXX…]` (BMP values, four hex digits each) or as
654/// `uXXXX` to `uXXXXXX`. A component it can't map, or a `uni` component with any group that
655/// isn't a character, adds nothing; `None` when nothing is left.
656pub(crate) fn glyph_name_to_text(name: &str) -> Option<BfString> {
657    let hex = |h: &str| u32::from_str_radix(h, 16).ok().and_then(char::from_u32);
658    // The specification's digits are uppercase only (`uni20ac` maps to nothing, review on
659    // #3239).
660    let upper_hex = |d: &str| d.bytes().all(|b| matches!(b, b'0'..=b'9' | b'A'..=b'F'));
661    let base = name.split('.').next().unwrap_or_default();
662    let mut text = String::new();
663    for part in base.split('_') {
664        if let Some(s) = glyph_names::get(part) {
665            text.push_str(s);
666        } else if let Some(digits) = part.strip_prefix("uni").filter(|d| !d.is_empty() && d.len() % 4 == 0 && upper_hex(d)) {
667            // All ASCII, so every fourth byte is a char boundary. A group that isn't a
668            // character (a surrogate) makes the whole component map to nothing.
669            let chars: Option<String> = (0..digits.len()).step_by(4).map(|at| digits.get(at..at + 4).and_then(hex)).collect();
670            text.extend(chars);
671        } else if let Some(c) = part.strip_prefix('u').filter(|d| (4..=6).contains(&d.len()) && upper_hex(d)).and_then(hex) {
672            text.push(c);
673        }
674    }
675    let mut chars = text.chars();
676    match (chars.next(), chars.next()) {
677        (None, _) => None,
678        (Some(c), None) => Some(BfString::Char(c)),
679        _ => Some(BfString::String(text)),
680    }
681}
682
683/// PdfCraft patch: the numbers a glyph name that only numbers its glyph gives (`C39`, `G27`,
684/// `MT174`: one to three ASCII letters, then one to six decimal or hexadecimal digits), for
685/// every split into letters and digits, read in decimal and in hexadecimal (`GA9` is `G` with
686/// hex `A9`); nothing for any other name. Everything from the first `.` is dropped first, as
687/// `glyph_name_to_text` drops it.
688fn glyph_name_numbers(name: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = u32> + '_ {
689    let base = name.split('.').next().unwrap_or_default();
690    (1..=3).flat_map(move |prefix| {
691        // `from_str_radix` would also take a leading `+`: the number is digits only, and at
692        // most six of them (a code is under 256, leading zeros as in `C0032`).
693        let digits = base.get(..prefix).zip(base.get(prefix..)).and_then(|(letters, digits)| {
694            (letters.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphabetic()) && (1..=6).contains(&digits.len()) && digits.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit()))
695                .then_some(digits)
696        });
697        digits.into_iter().flat_map(|d| [10, 16].into_iter().filter_map(move |radix| u32::from_str_radix(d, radix).ok()))
698    })
699}
700
701/// PdfCraft patch: whether every glyph name in a simple font's encoding that only numbers its
702/// glyph (see `glyph_name_numbers`) names the very code it sits at, in decimal or hexadecimal.
703/// Names the glyph list or its `uni`/`u` forms read are not numbered names. A font whose names
704/// number something else (`/Differences [1 /C70 /C105 …]`, a glyph's order in the subset)
705/// fails, and so does one where a single name numbers another code: there a name that happens
706/// to match its code (`/MT40` at 0x40, `/C1` at 233 beside `/C70` at 70, review on #3239) is a
707/// coincidence, not evidence. A subset that counts its glyphs in order of first use from code 1
708/// (`/Differences [1 /C1 /C2 … /C80]`) names its own codes too, but the counter says nothing
709/// about the characters (`/C65` is the 65th glyph used, not `A`): a numbered name at a C0
710/// control code (below 32), which no text shows, gives such a counter away and fails the font.
711pub(crate) fn numbered_names_name_their_codes<'a>(names: impl IntoIterator<Item = (u8, &'a str)>) -> bool {
712    names
713        .into_iter()
714        .filter(|(_, name)| glyph_names::get(name).is_none() && unicode_from_name(name).is_none() && glyph_name_to_text(name).is_none())
715        .all(|(code, name)| {
716            let mut numbers = glyph_name_numbers(name).peekable();
717            numbers.peek().is_none() || (code >= 0x20 && numbers.any(|n| n == u32::from(code)))
718        })
719}
720
721/// PdfCraft patch: the text of a glyph name outside the glyph list that only numbers its glyph
722/// (see `glyph_name_numbers`) when that number is the very code the glyph is shown with: the
723/// code's Latin-1 character, for codes above 127 too (`C174` reads `®`), as pdftotext, PDFium
724/// and MuPDF read it. The name and the code then agree, so nothing is guessed from an
725/// encoding table. A number naming another code (`/C1` at 233, review on #3239) and a control
726/// character read as nothing. Callers apply it only in a font where
727/// `numbered_names_name_their_codes` holds.
728pub(crate) fn numbered_glyph_name_at_its_code(name: &str, code: u8) -> Option<BfString> {
729    let c = char::from(code);
730    if c.is_control() {
731        return None;
732    }
733    glyph_name_numbers(name).any(|n| n == u32::from(code)).then_some(BfString::Char(c))
734}
735
736/// PdfCraft patch (92): the character a `uniXXXX` or `uXXXX` to `uXXXXXX` glyph name stands
737/// for, by the Adobe Glyph List Specification: `uni` and exactly four uppercase hex digits, or
738/// `u` and four to six; a value in the surrogate range or past U+10FFFF is no character. The
739/// text of a glyph goes by this rule, so `uni65`, `uni20ac` and `u41` read as nothing, as they
740/// do in [`glyph_name_to_text`].
741pub(crate) fn agl_unicode_from_name(name: &str) -> Option<char> {
742    let upper_hex = |d: &str| d.bytes().all(|b| matches!(b, b'0'..=b'9' | b'A'..=b'F'));
743    let digits = name
744        .strip_prefix("uni")
745        .filter(|d| d.len() == 4)
746        .or_else(|| name.strip_prefix('u').filter(|d| (4..=6).contains(&d.len())))
747        .filter(|d| upper_hex(d))?;
748    u32::from_str_radix(digits, 16).ok().and_then(char::from_u32)
749}
750
751/// Upstream's lenient reading of a `uni…` or `u…` name (any number of hex digits, either case),
752/// kept for finding a glyph in a font: PdfCraft patch (92) reads text by
753/// [`agl_unicode_from_name`] instead.
754pub(crate) fn unicode_from_name(name: &str) -> Option<char> {
755    let convert = |input: &str| u32::from_str_radix(input, 16).ok().and_then(char::from_u32);
756
757    name.starts_with("uni")
758        .then(|| name.get(3..).and_then(convert))
759        .or_else(|| name.starts_with("u").then(|| name.get(1..).and_then(convert)))
760        .flatten()
761}
762
763pub(crate) fn read_to_unicode(dict: &Dict<'_>, cmap_resolver: &CMapResolverFn) -> Option<CMap> {
764    dict.get::<Stream<'_>>(TO_UNICODE)
765        .and_then(|s| s.decoded().ok())
766        // See PDFJS-11915, where `Identity-H` is used for `ToUnicode`. I don't
767        // believe it's valid, but at least mupdf seems to be able to deal with it.
768        .or_else(|| {
769            dict.get::<Name<'_>>(TO_UNICODE).and_then(|name| (cmap_resolver)(CMapName::from_bytes(name.as_ref()))).map(|d| Cow::Owned(d.to_vec()))
770        })
771        .and_then(|data| {
772            let cmap_resolver = cmap_resolver.clone();
773            CMap::parse(&data, move |name| (cmap_resolver)(name))
774        })
775}

777// When mapping to glyphs, some fonts might only have a glyph for the "normalized"
778// name.
779pub(crate) fn normalized_glyph_name(mut name: &str) -> &str {
780    if name == "nbspace" {
781        name = "space";
782    }
783
784    if name == "sfthyphen" {
785        name = "hyphen";
786    }
787
788    name
789}
